document_purpose: Master, source-verified reference for all vehicle physical parameters and mesh sources used in Can It Ford. Every number below was pulled live from a primary source in this session (not from any NHTSA_vPIC_JSON file in the project, those contain zero physical data, confirmed by direct inspection). This supersedes vehicle_class_research_summary_2026-07-21.json.
important_note: This data previously existed only inside a Claude.ai chat conversation. It was not saved anywhere durable. This file fixes that.

part_1_L1_AR&R_threshold_vehicles.source: SAE Technical Paper 1999-01-1336 (Heydinger et al. 1999), DOI 10.4271/1999-01-1336, public PDF at eng.auburn.edu/~dmbevly/mech4420/vehicle_params.pdf, fetched live this session
part_1_L1_AR&R_threshold_vehicles.note: Weight figures are actual VIMF-measured TEST weight, driver-only condition unless noted. Driver is already included, do not add driver mass on top.

dodge_neon_1998.VIN_in_printed_paper: not published, printed table has no VINs for any 1998 VIMF vehicle

honda_crv_1998.class: proposed 4th class, small footprint / high clearance, NOT yet confirmed added to project

part_1_L1_AR&R_threshold_vehicles.vin_availability: The paper's own text states VINs exist only in an internal electronic copy, obtainable by contacting Dr. W. Riley Garrott, NHTSA/VRTC, riley.garrott@nhtsa.dot.gov. The printed table has zero VINs for any 1998 vehicle. This applies equally to all four vehicles above, it is not a CR-V-specific or RAV4-specific gap.

part_2_L2_MPM_mesh_vehicles_NCAC_CCSA.source: Center for Collision Safety and Analysis, George Mason University, ccsa.gmu.edu/models/, fetched live this session. Reverse-engineered from real, physically torn-down vehicles under NHTSA/FHWA contract.
part_2_L2_MPM_mesh_vehicles_NCAC_CCSA.note: These are NOT the same specific vehicles as Part 1 (no current NCAC model exists for a 1998 Neon, Explorer, or C1500). Recommended as the mesh-plus-physics source for the actual L2 render, self-consistent trio, real VIN and tire data where available.

sedan_2010_toyota_yaris.FLAG: Project currently computes rho using 1100kg (MASH class nominal target). This NCAC page states actual modeled weight is 1078kg, about 2 percent lower. Consider recomputing rho = 1078 / 3.5427 = 304.28 kg/m3 if precision matters before publication.

suv_2020_nissan_rogue.only_one_version_listed_on_page: no separate coarse variant currently shown, may need manual decimation for MPM particle seeding

still_open_after_this_file: Rogue coarse/decimated mesh variant, only the large 3.24M-element version was found on the live page, worth a follow-up check for a lighter version
Rogue tire size, not published on this page, would need a separate manufacturer spec lookup

Silverado and Rogue mass/CG/inertia values above are curb-condition test weight from the vehicle description table, not broken into CG height or moments of inertia the way SAE 1999-01-1336 does, those may exist inside the linked NCAC validation PDFs (2012-W-003 etc.) but were not opened this session
Tire rubber composition and wet/submerged-pavement friction coefficient, genuinely not covered by NCAC pages, still needs a literature pull
Whether to keep Neon/Explorer/C1500 as the L1 AR&R classification vehicles while using Yaris/Silverado/Rogue as the separate L2 mesh trio, or unify to one set, is a decision, not yet made
